Open, hide and quit groups of apps from the menu bar / system tray, with one shortcut per group.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | `…_x64-setup.exe` (or `…_x64_en-US.msi`) |
| **Linux · Ubuntu / Debian** | `…_amd64.deb` (ARM: `…_arm64.deb`) |
| **Linux · Fedora** | `…x86_64.rpm` (ARM: `…aarch64.rpm`) |
| **Linux · any distro** | `…_amd64.AppImage` (ARM: `…_aarch64.AppImage`) |
| **macOS · Apple silicon** | `…_aarch64.dmg` |

## Install

- **Windows:** run the installer. If Windows says *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info → Run anyway** (the app isn't code-signed yet).
- **Ubuntu / Debian:** `sudo apt install ./Jump.Starter_*_amd64.deb`
- **Fedora:** `sudo dnf install ./Jump.Starter-*.rpm`
- **AppImage:** `chmod +x Jump.Starter_*.AppImage`, then open it.
  On GNOME, install the *AppIndicator* extension so the tray icon shows.
- **macOS:** open the .dmg and drag the app to Applications. The first time, allow it in
  **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** (not notarized yet).

## Default shortcuts

| | Windows / macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Open group N | Ctrl+N | Ctrl+Alt+N |
| Hide / show group N | Ctrl+Alt+N | Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N |
| Quit group N | Ctrl+Shift+N | — |
